title: medhelm
summary: MedHELM is a comprehensive medical AI benchmark suite that evaluates language models on diverse healthcare tasks including clinical QA, medical dialogue, EHR analysis, and clinical note generation. It provides end-to-end infrastructure for scenario definition, model adaptation, inference execution, metric computation, and result visualization across single and multi-GPU environments.

nodes.label: Researcher / Developer
nodes.title: Human user
nodes.description: Defines benchmarks, configures runs, executes evaluations, and analyzes results through the MedHELM system.

nodes.label: Orchestrate Benchmark Runs
nodes.title: Run orchestration
nodes.description: Coordinates end-to-end benchmark execution from specification through result generation. Manages single-GPU, multi-GPU, and SLURM-based job scheduling with support for re-evaluation workflows.

nodes.label: Define Run Specifications
nodes.title: Run configuration
nodes.description: Specifies benchmark configurations including model selection, adapter settings, and evaluation parameters. Factory functions generate task-specific run specs for medical and general benchmarks.

nodes.label: Load Scenarios and Data
nodes.title: Data loading
nodes.description: Retrieves and preprocesses benchmark scenarios and test data. Supports diverse medical datasets (clinical QA, EHR, dialogue) and general-purpose benchmarks with optional data augmentation.

nodes.label: Adapt Models to Tasks
nodes.title: Model adaptation
nodes.description: Applies task-specific adapters to prepare models for evaluation. Handles prompt engineering, in-context learning, and input formatting for different task types.

nodes.label: Apply Data Augmentations
nodes.title: Robustness testing
nodes.description: Applies text perturbations (typos, contractions, dialect shifts, gender terms) to test model robustness across input variations and demographic fairness.

nodes.label: Execute Model Inference
nodes.title: Inference execution
nodes.description: Executes inference across language models, vision-language models, audio models, and image generation services. Abstracts API differences and manages token counting and cost estimation.

nodes.label: Compute Performance Metrics
nodes.title: Metric calculation
nodes.description: Calculates quantitative metrics (accuracy, BLEU, F1, etc.) on model outputs. Supports classification, generation, summarization, and image quality assessment across task types.

nodes.label: Manage Annotations
nodes.title: Annotation workflow
nodes.description: Orchestrates human and automated annotation processes. Handles annotator selection, result aggregation, and quality control for evaluation tasks.

nodes.label: Present Results
nodes.title: Result presentation
nodes.description: Generates visualizations, interactive dashboards, and comprehensive evaluation reports. Produces JSON, HTML, and summary documents for stakeholder review.

nodes.label: Provide Infrastructure Services
nodes.title: Infrastructure support
nodes.description: Supplies tokenization, proxy services, window management, logging, and utilities. Enables distributed execution, remote communication, and token cost tracking.

groups.label: User Interaction
groups.title: User entry point
groups.description: Researchers and developers interact with MedHELM to define, execute, and analyze medical AI benchmarks.

groups.label: Orchestration
groups.title: Execution control
groups.description: Manages overall benchmark workflow and coordinates all downstream components through specifications and run lifecycle management.

groups.label: Data Preparation
groups.title: Input setup
groups.description: Loads medical scenarios, adapts models for task-specific evaluation, and applies robustness augmentations to test fairness and resilience.

groups.label: Execution and Evaluation
groups.title: Core processing

groups.label: Output and Support
groups.title: Results and infrastructure
groups.description: Presents results through visualizations and reports while providing underlying infrastructure for tokenization, proxies, and distributed execution.
